title: Tourism Quiz Challenge – Cambridge Global English Stage 9, Unit 3: Tourism

p1.title: The Lost Passport
p1.text:
Last summer, Amira and her parents were travelling around Italy by train. On their third day, they were sightseeing in Rome. While they were queuing outside the Colosseum, Amira noticed that her father looked worried. He was searching through every pocket of his jacket.

His passport was missing! The family hurried back to their hotel. When they arrived, the receptionist smiled and held up a small red booklet. A waiter had found the passport on the breakfast table, and it was being kept safely at the front desk.

“I was so relieved,” Amira’s father said later. “That waiter turned a stressful morning into a funny story we will always remember.”

p2.title: A Morning in Sidi Bou Said
p2.text:
Perched on a cliff above the Gulf of Tunis, Sidi Bou Said is one of the most photographed villages in Tunisia. Its white walls and bright blue doors and windows attract visitors from all over the world.

When I visited last spring, the narrow streets were full of life. Artists were painting at their easels, and tourists were taking photos of almost every doorway. In a small café at the top of the hill, mint tea with pine nuts was being served while a musician was playing the oud.

Some local people worry that the village is becoming too crowded. They want tourism to be managed carefully so that the village keeps its peaceful character.

p3.title: Green Island Eco-Lodge
p3.text:
Green Island Eco-Lodge was opened ten years ago by a small group of local families. Unlike large resort hotels, the lodge has only twelve cabins, and they were built from local wood by island carpenters.

Guests are encouraged to take part in conservation projects. Last month, while a group of students was staying at the lodge, baby turtles were being released on the beach every night. The students helped the rangers to count the turtles and keep the beach clean.

Electricity at the lodge comes from solar panels, and rainwater is collected for the showers. Some guests find the simple cabins a little uncomfortable, but most say that the experience is worth it.

p4.title: A Tour Guide’s Diary
p4.text:
Monday, 14 July. Today was my first day as a guide at the National Museum. Unfortunately, the main hall was being renovated, so my group could not see the famous mosaics there. While the workers were repairing the roof, I showed the visitors the ancient coins and jewellery upstairs.

At lunchtime, a German couple asked me for directions to the old medina. I drew them a small map and recommended a traditional restaurant near the main gate.

At the end of the afternoon, I was thanked by the whole group for an interesting tour. I was exhausted, but very proud of myself.

questions.text: What were Amira and her parents doing when her father started to look worried?
questions.explanation: The text says: “While they were queuing outside the Colosseum, Amira noticed that her father looked worried.”

questions.text: Where was the passport being kept?
questions.explanation: The passport “was being kept safely at the front desk” of the hotel.

questions.text: In the last paragraph, the word “relieved” means…
options: happy because a worry has gone
questions.explanation: You feel relieved when something you were worried about ends well – the passport was found.

questions.text: What can we infer about the waiter?
options: He was a friend of the family
questions.explanation: He found the passport and gave it to reception instead of keeping it, so we can infer he was honest and helpful.

questions.text: According to the passage, why do visitors come to Sidi Bou Said?
options: Its white walls and blue doors and windows
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says the white walls and bright blue doors and windows attract visitors from all over the world.

questions.text: What was happening in the café at the top of the hill?
options: Artists were painting the café walls
Mint tea was being served while a musician played
Tourists were cooking their own lunch
questions.explanation: “Mint tea with pine nuts was being served while a musician was playing the oud.”

questions.text: The word “perched” suggests that the village is…
options: built high up, on the edge of a cliff
questions.explanation: “Perched on a cliff” means sitting high up on the edge of something, like a bird on a branch.

questions.text: What is the main worry of some local people?
options: Too many visitors could spoil the village’s peaceful character
The streets are too narrow for cars
The café prices are too high
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says they worry the village is becoming too crowded and want it to keep its peaceful character.

questions.text: Who opened Green Island Eco-Lodge?
options: A small group of local families
questions.explanation: “Green Island Eco-Lodge was opened ten years ago by a small group of local families.”

questions.text: What was happening on the beach every night last month?
options: The students were having a party
A new cabin was being built
questions.explanation: “Baby turtles were being released on the beach every night” – past continuous passive.

questions.text: Which statement about the lodge is TRUE?
options: Its electricity comes from the sun
It has more than one hundred rooms
It was built by a foreign company
questions.explanation: The text says electricity comes from solar panels. It has only twelve cabins, built by island carpenters, and guests are encouraged to help.

questions.text: Which word best describes the lodge’s approach to tourism?
questions.explanation: Solar power, collected rainwater, local materials and conservation projects all show a sustainable approach.

questions.text: Why couldn’t the group see the famous mosaics?
options: The main hall was being renovated
The museum is closed on Mondays
questions.explanation: “The main hall was being renovated, so my group could not see the famous mosaics.”

questions.text: What did the guide do for the German couple?
options: Drew them a map and recommended a restaurant
questions.explanation: The guide “drew them a small map and recommended a traditional restaurant”.

questions.text: How did the guide feel at the end of the day?
questions.explanation: “Exhausted” means very tired, and the guide says “very proud of myself”.

questions.text: We ________ a boat trip around the island yesterday.
questions.explanation: “Yesterday” shows a finished past action, so we use the past simple: took.

questions.text: At 9 o’clock last night, we ________ dinner on the hotel terrace.
questions.explanation: We use the past continuous for an action in progress at a specific time in the past.

questions.text: While the tourists ________ the museum, it started to rain.
questions.explanation: The longer background action uses the past continuous. “Tourists” is plural, so we need “were visiting”.

questions.text: When we arrived at the hotel, the swimming pool ________.
questions.explanation: The pool doesn’t clean itself, so we need the passive. The action was in progress: past continuous passive = was being + past participle.

questions.text: The old bridge ________ when we visited the town, so we had to take a ferry.
questions.explanation: Workers were repairing the bridge at that time; the bridge receives the action, so we use the past continuous passive.

questions.text: Choose the passive form of: “The guide was showing the visitors the castle.”
options: The visitors were shown the castle by the guide.
The guide was being shown the castle.
The visitors were being shown the castle by the guide.
The visitors are being shown the castle by the guide.
questions.explanation: Past continuous active (was showing) becomes past continuous passive (were being shown). The tense must stay the same.

questions.text: Find the mistake: “While I was walking along the beach, I was finding a beautiful shell.”
questions.explanation: Finding the shell is a short, completed action that interrupts the walk, so it should be past simple: “I found a beautiful shell.”

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
options: The rooms were being cleaned when we checked in.
The rooms was being cleaned when we checked in.
The rooms were being clean when we checked in.
The rooms were cleaning when we checked in.
questions.explanation: Plural subject → were; passive → being + past participle (cleaned).

questions.text: “Thousands of photos are taken at the Eiffel Tower every day.” This sentence is…
questions.explanation: are + past participle (taken) = present simple passive. We don’t need to say who takes the photos.

questions.text: Our flight ________ because of the storm.
questions.explanation: The airline cancelled the flight; the flight receives the action, so we use the passive: was cancelled.

questions.text: What ________ you ________ when the fire alarm went off?
questions.explanation: We ask about an action in progress when something else happened, so we use the past continuous: “What were you doing?”

questions.text: The tourists ________ around the old town by a local guide when the storm began.
questions.explanation: The tourists received the action (passive) and it was in progress (continuous). Plural subject → were being guided.

questions.text: A person whose job is to show tourists around a place and give information is a…
questions.explanation: A tour guide leads visitors and explains things. A travel agent sells trips; a receptionist works at a hotel desk.

questions.text: The word “accommodation” means…
questions.explanation: Accommodation is somewhere to stay, such as a hotel, hostel, campsite or holiday apartment.

questions.text: Which document must you show at border control when you travel to another country?
questions.explanation: A passport proves your identity and nationality when you cross a border.

questions.text: An “itinerary” is…
options: a detailed plan of a journey
questions.explanation: An itinerary lists where you will go and when – the plan of your trip.

questions.text: Which word means “a famous building or place that is easy to recognise”?
questions.explanation: A landmark, like the Eiffel Tower or the Colosseum, is easy to recognise. A landscape is the view of an area of land.

questions.text: We bought a small model of the Eiffel Tower as a ________ of our trip.
questions.explanation: A souvenir is something you buy or keep to remember a place you visited.

questions.text: “Ecotourism” is tourism that…
options: protects nature and helps local people
only takes place in big cities
questions.explanation: Ecotourism means responsible travel to natural areas that protects the environment and supports local communities.

questions.text: The hotel was fully booked, so there were no ________.
questions.explanation: Vacancies are free rooms. “No vacancies” means the hotel is full.

questions.text: An “excursion” is…
options: the bill you pay at a hotel
a long delay at the airport
a short trip for pleasure, often with a group
questions.explanation: An excursion is a short journey made for pleasure, for example a day trip to the desert or a boat trip.
